time limit per test 2 seconds
memory limit per test 256 megabytes

You are given a sequence of integers \(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n\) and an integer \(k\). Your task is to find the longest contiguous subarray such that every element appears at most \(k\) times in it.

More formally, find the maximal segment \([l, r]\) such that for every value \(v\), the number of occurrences of \(v\) inside the segment does not exceed \(k\). The classic two-pointer technique solves this in linear time because $$\sum_{i=1}^{n} (r_i - l_i + 1) \le n$$ holds for every monotone scan of the array.

The proof of the upper bound uses the geometric series: if each step contributes at least half of the remaining length, the total work is bounded by $$\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} 2^{-j} = 2$$ which is constant per element.

  • The first pointer advances while the constraint is satisfied and the current sum stays below \(s\).
  • The second pointer contracts the window whenever the constraint \(c_i \le m\) is violated.

Output the length of the longest valid segment and its left endpoint; if several answers exist, print the leftmost one. Note that \(n \le 2 \cdot 10^{5}\) so an \(O(n \log n)\) solution is sufficient.
